title: Quarterly bridgework playbook: compatibility & activation for Private/VPC/On‑Prem
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective:
Build a pragmatic, repeatable playbook for the quarter that sequences compatibility work (networking, KMS, RBAC, upgrade windows) and activation cohorts for Private/VPC/On‑Prem customers. The goal is to reduce activation lead time to <= 6 weeks for standard cohorts and eliminate 80% of custom compatibility blockers encountered in recent pilots.

Scope:
- Compatibility matrix and prioritization rules for networking topologies (VPC peering, PrivateLink, NAT), KMS/HSM integrations, and supported upgrade windows.
- Activation cohort framework: lighthouse customers, early adopters, standard cohort.
- Experimentation lanes: dark-launch test harnesses, canary migration checklist, rollback criteria.
- Risk and contingency playbooks (capacity hedges, fallback to hosted models, emergency rollback).

Why now:
Multiple enterprise pilots stalled on small but high-latency compatibility gaps. Without a clear, codified playbook we repeatedly re-discuss the same integration items per-customer which increases TTM and ops cost. This playbook translates cross-team tacit knowledge into a set of deterministic gates, automation tasks, and acceptance criteria that PMs, Eng, and Solutions can follow.

Success metrics (OKR mapping):
- OKR-PVT-1: Reduce average activation time for standard cohort from 11 weeks to <= 6 weeks (metric: calendar days from contract to first-serving production requests).
- OKR-PVT-2: Decrease number of compatibility blockers reported post-onboarding by 80% for new customers in the cohort.
- OKR-REL-3: 90% of activations follow the playbook steps (tracked via activation checklist completion).

Deliverables this quarter:
1) Compatibility decision matrix (networking/KMS/upgrade): PDF & live Confluence table.
2) Activation cohort definitions + canned onboarding task list in runway template.
3) Canary checklist + rollback runbook (Ops runbook + playbook for Solutions Eng).
4) Automation backlog (3 Jira/Linear tickets) to preflight common checks (DNS, certs, KMS policy templates).
5) Postmortem template to capture learnings and feed into Optimize heuristics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compatibility matrix published in Confluence with owner and risk band for each cell.
- Runbook validated with at least 2 pilot customers (lighthouse + standard) and checklist used end-to-end.
- Automation backlog items scoped and triaged with eng owners; at least 1 preflight check delivered by release cut.
- Stakeholder alignment: Security, Infra, Solutions, and Sales have reviewed and signed-off on portability gates.

Risks and mitigations:
- Heavy engineering demand for preflight checks -> mitigation: narrow initial scope to top 5 failure modes and provide manual runbook for the rest.
- Customer network heterogeneity -> mitigation: define three supported network topologies and clear out-of-scope list.
- SLAs on Dedicated capacity -> mitigation: coordinate with Capacity/Eng to reserve soft buffer for activation windows.

Links & artifacts:
- PRD (draft): https://docs.google.com/document/d/PRD-bridgework-playbook
- Confluence compatibility matrix (working): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/x/compat-matrix
- Onboarding checklist template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/onboard-templates
- Related Linear tickets: PM-74216 (parent), ENG-84122 (preflight checks scope)
